Content: “I journeyed to the country of the Uighur Turks on relay horses which their ruler sent me and I was traveling as fast as I could. I journeyed `text(twenty days)` in steppes where there were springs and grass but no villages or towns, only the men of the horse relay service living in tents. And after that I traveled another `text(twenty days)` among villages. The people living there were all Turks, and among them were fire-worshippers professing the Zoroastrian religion as well as polytheists. After all these `text(days)` I arrived at the king's town. The king of the Uighurs is related by marriage to the king of China, and the latter is sending him yearly `500text(,)000` loads of silk.

On the road to the Uighur Khanate, I passed through the Muslim city of Samarkand. I was told that God had granted victory to the ruler of Samarkand over the king of China. The king of Samarkand defeated the king of China and killed many of his companions. The Muslims took enormous plunder and captured some people whose children fabricate in Samarkand good paper and various kinds of arms and implements. These are produced only in Samarkand.”
Copyright: Tamim al-Muttawwi'i, Muslim traveler from the Abbasid Caliphate, account of his journey in Central Asia, `text(ninth century C.E.)`
